title: TWICE AS MUCH ON THE SIXTH DAY

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much-two omers for each person-and the
leaders of the community came and reported this to Moses. He said to them, 'This
is what the LORD commanded: "Tomorrow is to be a day of sabbath rest, a holy
sabbath to the LORD. So bake what you want to bake and boil what you want to
boil. Save whatever is left and keep it until morning."'" - Ex 16:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The leaders come to Moses puzzled. Twice as much has appeared. What does it
mean?

Moses explains: tomorrow is a Sabbath.

Notice that the double portion came before the explanation. God provided first,
and the reason became clear afterwards. That is often how it works. We receive
something unexpected and only later understand what it was for.

Notice also the practical instruction: bake what you want to bake, boil what you
want to boil, today. Preparation on Saturday is what makes Sunday restful, to
put it in our terms. Rest does not happen accidentally. It is planned for.

Anyone who has tried to protect a day of rest knows this. If nothing is prepared,
the day fills with the tasks that were left undone. Genuine rest usually costs
some work beforehand.

This is not legalism. Paul is clear that believers should not judge one another
over sacred days (Col 2:16). But the principle beneath the Sabbath is God's gift
to human beings, not a burden. We are creatures, not machines, and we were made
to stop.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you prepare for rest, or just hope it happens?
2. What would you need to do beforehand to genuinely stop for a day?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You for providing ahead of my need. Help me to plan for rest and
receive it as Your gift rather than earning my way through every day. Amen.
